questions: For each i, are we required to choose exactly K elements that include A_i, or at least K elements?
When choosing K elements that include A_i, can we choose any K elements from the entire sequence, or must they be contiguous or have some other restriction?
For each i, should we output the maximum possible GCD among all valid choices of K elements including A_i, or the GCD of a specific set (e.g., the first K elements including A_i)?
If multiple valid choices of K elements including A_i exist, should we output the GCD for each choice separately, or a single value (e.g., the average or sum)?
Does 'include A_i' mean we must include the element at position i exactly once, or can we include other elements with the same value as A_i from different positions?
Should the output be a single line with N space-separated integers, one for each i, or N lines each with one integer?
Is the GCD defined as the greatest positive integer dividing all chosen elements, and what should be output if the GCD is 0 (e.g., if all chosen elements are 0)?
If K = 1, does 'choose K elements that include A_i' mean we must choose exactly A_i itself, so the GCD is just A_i?
